source_anchor: CLRS §2.1 insertion sort / §2.3 merge sort (general comparison-sort correctness); MDN Array.prototype.sort numeric comparator
prompt_text: Sort the array [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6] in ascending numeric order and print it as JSON. Expected output: "[1,1,2,3,4,5,6,9]".

candidate_responses.text: CORRECT: non-mutating spread-then-sort with the same (a,b)=>a-b comparator.
WRONG: single bubble-sort pass only swaps adjacent pairs once, leaving the array unsorted (a full bubble sort needs n-1 passes).
candidate_responses.code: const a=[3,1,4,1,5,9,2,6]; for(let i=0;i<a.length-1;i++){if(a[i]>a[i+1]){const t=a[i]; a[i]=a[i+1]; a[i+1]=t;}} console.log(JSON.stringify(a));

candidate_responses.text: CARGO-CULT: uses sort with (a,b)=>... comparator and spread copy, but the comparator sign is flipped so the array sorts descending.
